m.title: SQL Queries
m.q: Using Pupils(ID, Name, Mark): 101 Ada 72; 102 Ben 43; 103 Mia 81. Write SQL to return the names of pupils with Mark >= 50, and state the result.
st: SELECT Name: ask for the Name field, not the complete record.
FROM Pupils: identify the table holding these rows.
WHERE Mark >= 50: Ada (72) and Mia (81) match; Ben (43) does not.
SELECT Name FROM Pupils WHERE Mark >= 50; returns Ada and Mia, in no guaranteed order unless an ordering rule is specified.

k.q: Predict the output, then connect the condition to SQL WHERE Mark >= 50.
k.code:
mark = 43
if mark >= 50 then
    print("Include")
else
    print("Exclude")
endif
p: Explain your predicted result using the first assignment or test.
Change mark to 72 and predict the output.
Change the program so it displays 'Ada' when mark is 72 and 'Ben' when mark is 43; explain that SQL SELECT chooses what field is returned.
k.a: Initially Exclude; mark=72 prints Include. A simple additional selection can print Ada/Ben for this small known dataset; SQL SELECT Name returns the corresponding name field without hard-coding individual marks.

e: Write SQL to return Name from Pupils where Mark > 70. [3 marks]
SELECT Name [1] FROM Pupils [1] WHERE Mark > 70 [1]; result Ada and Mia.
For the shared table, what value is returned by SELECT Name FROM Pupils WHERE ID = 103;? [2 marks]
Mia [1]; because the row with ID 103 matches the WHERE condition [1].
Explain how SELECT and WHERE perform different jobs in SELECT Name FROM Pupils WHERE Mark < 50; [3 marks]
SELECT Name chooses the field to output [1]; WHERE Mark < 50 filters qualifying rows [1]; in this dataset only Ben matches [1].

stretch.task: Use Pupils(ID,Name,Mark). Write a query for the names with marks below 60. State the exact result and explain why Ada is excluded.
stretch.hint: SELECT Name FROM Pupils WHERE Mark < 60;
stretch.answer: Ben is returned because 43 < 60. Ada's 72 and Mia's 81 do not pass. SQL: SELECT Name FROM Pupils WHERE Mark < 60;

mastery.task: Explain how a loop and IF could reproduce SELECT Name FROM Pupils WHERE Mark >= 50. Using parallel numeric marks and names arrays, write the code and compare its output to SQL.
mastery.hint: for i=0 to 2: IF marks[i]>=50 THEN print(names[i]). A SQL result is not guaranteed to be ordered without ORDER BY.
mastery.answer: For names=[Ada,Ben,Mia] and marks=[72,43,81], code prints Ada then Mia. The SQL result contains Ada and Mia; row ordering is not guaranteed unless explicitly requested.
